head: Term
Meaning
Example
rows: Audit
A structured check of where energy enters, is used, and might be reduced.
An auditor compares a site schedule with its meter data.
Scope
The buildings, systems, period, and decisions included in an audit.
A scope can exclude fleet fuel from a building-only review.
Audit level
How deeply the audit measures and analyses a site.
An initial review uses fewer measurements than a detailed study.
Baseline
Reference use expected under stated conditions.
Compare later loads with a typical operating schedule.
Energy
Total amount used or delivered.
A motor consumes 40 kWh during an operating period.
Power
Energy flow rate at one time or interval.
A pump draws 6 kW while running.
kW
Kilowatt, a unit of power.
A load rated 2 kW uses energy while switched on.
kWh
Kilowatt-hour, a unit of energy.
A 2 kW load over 3 hours uses 6 kWh.
GJ
Gigajoule, a unit of energy.
1,000 kWh corresponds to 3.6 GJ.
Demand
Maximum averaged use rate within a defined billing interval.
A utility can bill the highest 15-minute average.
Load factor
Average power divided by peak power in the same period.
A steady load has a higher factor than a short spike.
Power factor
Real electrical power divided by apparent electrical power.
An inductive motor can have a factor below 1.
Energy use intensity
Annual energy divided by building area; often called EUI.
2,000 GJ across 4,000 m2 is 0.5 GJ/m2-year.
EUI
Short name for energy use intensity.
Use one EUI basis when comparing two offices.
Site energy
Energy shown as delivered use at the property.
An electricity meter measures supplied kWh.
Source energy
Energy basis accounting for upstream production and delivery.
Electricity may use a source multiplier above 1.
Source multiplier
Factor converting site energy to a specified source basis.
The exercise uses 1.98 for purchased electricity.
Diversity factor
Allowance for equipment not running at full load together.
Several compressors can have a lower joint peak.
Time-of-use
A price that depends on when energy is used.
A unit can cost more in a peak period.
Simple payback
Initial cost divided by annual net savings.
A $500 project saving $250 per year pays back in 2 years.
Net present value
Discounted future net benefits less initial cost, or NPV.
A project may have positive NPV at one chosen rate.
IRR
Internal rate of return; a rate producing zero NPV.
Compare IRR with the appropriate investment requirement.
Life-cycle cost
Cost across the chosen ownership period.
Include upkeep as well as the purchase.
EnPI
Energy performance indicator tied to activity or output.
A plant tracks kWh per product unit.
Regression
A method for estimating energy dependence on drivers.
Energy can vary with outdoor temperature.
CUSUM
Cumulative sum of differences from expected use.
A trend upward signals a persistent difference.
EEM
Energy efficiency measure, a proposed change to reduce energy.
Repairing a fan schedule can be an EEM.
Lighting efficacy
Light output per unit of electrical power.
Compare lumens per watt among lamps.
Lumens
A unit describing visible light output.
Two lamps can emit different lumens at equal watts.
Lighting power density
Installed lighting power per floor area.
Divide fixture watts by illuminated square metres.
HVAC
Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning.
A rooftop HVAC system heats, cools, or ventilates.
COP
Coefficient of performance; useful heat transfer divided by input power.
Cooling COP 4 means 4 kW cooling per kW input.
EER
Energy efficiency ratio in the stated unit convention.
Check the units before comparing EER with COP.
Boiler efficiency
Useful thermal output divided by fuel input.
70 GJ useful heat from 100 GJ fuel is 70%.
R value
Thermal resistance to heat flow.
A higher R means greater resistance.
U value
Thermal transmittance, the inverse of matching total R.
R of 5 gives U of 0.2 in matching SI units.
Infiltration
Unplanned airflow through a building enclosure.
A gap around a door can create heat loss.
Shaft power
Useful mechanical output of a motor.
A pump receives shaft power from its motor.
Variable frequency drive
A device controlling compatible motor speed.
A fan can vary speed with needed airflow.
Motor slip
Difference between synchronous and actual induction-motor speed.
A rotor may turn slightly slower than the field.
Compressed air
Air stored or delivered above atmospheric pressure.
A compressor runs to supply pneumatic tools.
Control point
One measured or commanded variable in a control system.
A control point can record fan status.
Trend log
Time-ordered readings from a control or meter.
A log shows whether a fan ran overnight.
M&V
Measurement and verification of the impact of a change.
Compare a retrofit with an adjusted baseline.
IPMVP
An energy savings measurement and verification protocol.
An auditor may choose an IPMVP method.
Cogeneration
One process supplying electricity and useful heat.
Recovered heat can serve a facility load.
Storage
Equipment holding energy for later use.
A battery can shift electricity demand.
Fleet indicator
Energy used per meaningful transport output.
A vehicle fleet tracks litres per 100 km.
Degree-days
A weather measure combining temperature difference and time.
Heating use can change with degree-days.
Psychrometrics
Analysis of the thermal and moisture state of air.
An air chart helps estimate cooling and drying.
Sensitivity analysis
Changing assumptions to see how a result shifts.
Recalculate payback at several operating-hour values.
Affinity laws
Approximate relations between pump or fan speed, flow, head, and power under similar operating conditions.
Ideal power ratio is the speed ratio cubed, if similarity assumptions hold.
Calibration
A documented check that relates an instrument reading to a known reference.
Verify meter calibration before using a small observed difference as evidence.
Latent load
Heating or cooling associated with a moisture change rather than temperature alone.
A cooling coil that removes humidity has a latent load.
